source.title: Capacitated Dominating Set on Planar Graphs

accepted.question_text: For unweighted splittable-demand hard-capacity Capacitated Domination on planar graphs, can the PTAS technique for bounded positive integer maximum demand and capacity be extended to arbitrary integral demands and capacities or to bounded real-valued demands and capacities while still approximating minimum-size feasible assignments that cover all vertex demand without exceeding vertex capacities?

evidence.quote: In this paper we consider the unweighted, splittable-demand, hard-capacity version of CDP with integral capacities and demands.
Most immediately, can we accommodate arbitrary integral or bounded real-valued demands and capacities?

accepted.question_text: For hard-capacity Capacitated Domination on planar graphs, can the solution technique be extended from uniform vertex weights to real non-negative vertex weights despite the difficulty that smoothing exchanges capacity for weight in unit quantities and may not bound the weight of an underfull vertex selected during reassignment?

evidence.quote: The weighted version has real, non-negative vertex weights whereas the unweighted version has uniform vertex weights of weight one.
Alternatively, can we extend the solution to the weighted case?

accepted.question_text: Can a smoothing or rounding variant for hard-capacity Capacitated Domination on planar graphs give a bicriteria approximation in which capacities may be exceeded by a small bounded amount or demands may be under-covered by a small bounded amount?

evidence.quote: Alternatively a careful rounding strategy may lead to a bicriteria result in which either the capacities can be exceeded or the demands can be under-covered by a small (bounded) amount.

accepted.question_text: For capacitated r-hop domination, where a chosen vertex can cover any vertex within graph distance r and CDP is the case r = 1, can the bounded-branchwidth dynamic program be extended without too many boundary configurations when demand of a non-boundary vertex in a cluster may be covered outside the cluster?

evidence.quote: One such problem is capacitated r-hop domination, in which a vertex can cover any vertex within a distance of r.

However, the dynamic program given in Section 4 does not readily extend to r-hop domination: demand of a non-boundary vertex in a cluster may be covered by a vertex outside of the cluster and encoding all possible ways in which demand can traverse the cluster boundary seems to generate too many configurations.

accepted.question_text: Can the techniques for hard-capacity Capacitated Domination on planar graphs be generalized to a broader class of hard-capacitated problems and to optimization problems where multiplicities are forbidden, so selected objects cannot simply be duplicated to absorb excess demand or capacity conflicts?

evidence.quote: We hope to generalize the techniques introduced here to apply to a broader range of (hard)-capacitated problems and other problems that forbid multiplicities.
